cards.explanation: The answer is True. The LORD says, “Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being…” (Isaiah 66:2). I make cookies one stamp at a time and my mustache gets tired. He made everything, and the question shows it. It comes right after He asks what kind of house you could build for Him.

The one the LORD will esteem is the humble one who trembles at His word. He says, “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). Notice He doesn't say the one with the biggest anything. I think that's good news for all of us, friends.

The answer is that they have chosen their own ways. Look at what verse 3 does: “Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man…” The offerings are right there, and the LORD still sets them beside awful things. Then He says what is going on: “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). So the problem isn't that they brought something. It's that they did it their own way and not His.

The answer is punishment. The LORD says, “So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them…” (Isaiah 66:4). They chose their ways, and now He chooses their punishment. This is a heavy verse, friends.

The answer is that He called and no one answered. The LORD says, “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). His reason isn't a missed rule, it's that nobody paid Him any mind. I think this part is heavy, friends. Then the verse says what they did instead: “But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

The answer is because of the LORD's name. The text says, “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name…” (Isaiah 66:5). It's said to those who tremble at His word. I think that has to sting, being shut out by your own brothers. The LORD sees it, though, and speaks to them directly.

The answer is that they will be put to shame. The brothers say, “Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!” and the LORD answers, “But they will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 66:5). It's a short sentence with a lot of weight in it. The ones who tremble at His word hear this straight from Him.

The answer is False. The verse says the voice from the temple is “…the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve!” (Isaiah 66:6). No watchmen are named. The voice belongs to the LORD Himself.

The answer is False. He doesn't say people hear about things like this all the time. He asks, “Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things?” (Isaiah 66:8). The questions show how astonishing this is. If I told you my cookies baked themselves before the oven warmed up, you'd ask the same thing.

The answer is Zion. The verse says, “Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.” (Isaiah 66:8). The picture is of Zion as a mother. She gives birth to her children, and it happens as soon as she is in labor.

The answer is that He will surely deliver it. The LORD asks, “Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” and then, “Or will I who deliver close the womb?” (Isaiah 66:9). Asked that way, the answer is no, He will not leave the birth undone. In this picture, He delivers.

The answer is True. The verse says, “Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her…” (Isaiah 66:10). So the call isn't only for those who are already happy. Those who mourn over her are told to rejoice too.

The answer is that they are carried on her arm. The LORD says, “you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees.” (Isaiah 66:12). It's a picture of little ones being held close. I'll admit, nobody ever carried me on an arm. I got slid into a drawer.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.” (Isaiah 66:13). Think of how a mother's comfort feels, friends. He says that's how He will comfort them. It's a tender verse.
The answer is grass. The verse says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). Not a tall tree, just grass. I think grass is a nice everyday picture.

The answer is False. The verse says, “then the hand of the LORD will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies.” (Isaiah 66:14). His servants see His hand. His wrath is shown to His enemies.
